Call it with the action_key BEFORE wiring a form to an action: never guess model names or field names.

Wire a form on the page to a form action, exactly like the editor's Action selector does: switches the form's model, renders the action's default fields, hidden defaults and success page, and/or sets hidden destination/preset field values. Returns the resulting form HTML, the form as it was before a switch (previous_form_html), and the action's destination fields with their candidate records so you can ask the user to choose. Call it after applying the form snippet and before adapting the fields. Never wire a form by hand (data-model_name or hidden dnone inputs).
Rules and tools for website forms: Any form whose submission does any kind of a backend action. Load BEFORE creating, editing, rewiring or removing any form on a page.

# Webforms A webform does a backend action on submission: it sends an email or creates a record. The action wired on the form decides WHICH. The "Get Webform Info" tool lists the available actions and, per action, the model fields a form input can bind to. ## Building a form - ALWAYS start from one of the droppable form snippets fetched with "Get Snippets": "s_title_form" (title above a simple form, the default choice), "s_form_aside" (form beside contact info), "s_website_form_cover" (form over a cover image). Adapt it; NEVER compose a form's structure from scratch. - Flow for a new form: apply the adapted snippet, wire it with "Set Form Action", resolve the destinations with the user, then adapt the rendered fields (texts, styling, extra fields). - Keep the form's wiring exactly as rendered and change only texts, styling and the fields themselves: every field wrapper's classes, every `data-*` attribute, and the submit block (including the empty and the a.s_website_form_send button) must survive your edits. - NEVER write a `website_form_signature` input: it is managed automatically and anything you write there is removed. - In those snippets the
is NESTED inside the snippet's own top-level section: KEEP that nesting. Never place a section carrying `s_website_form` directly at page level, and never merge its classes into your own section's root: nested, the user gets a clean separate "Form" panel in the editor; top-level or merged, the form options fuse with the section's. The nested form section's only content is the container holding the
(and the end message div); your titles, texts and images live in the wrapper section around it. ## Wiring the action - NEVER wire a form by hand, no editing `data-model_name`, no hand-written hidden dnone inputs. Call "Set Form Action": it does exactly what the editor's Action selector does (renders the action's fields, hidden defaults and success page) and returns the resulting form HTML plus the action's destination fields. - Destinations are where submissions end up (the recipient address, the record new entries attach to, ...). EVERY destination field the tool returns must be resolved WITH the user before the form is done: present the candidates and any prefilled value as the recommended choice with the Ask User Question tool, then call "Set Form Action" again with the approved values in `fields`. A prefilled or default value is NOT a user choice: even when the tool result shows a destination already filled in, you must still ask. Never choose a destination yourself, never leave a required destination unset, and never invent a value. - In any form HTML you write, leave the recipient (`email_to`) value EMPTY. A recipient only ever comes from the user: ask (the company address from "Get Webform Info" is the choice to recommend), then set the approved address with "Set Form Action". Never write, guess or reuse an address the user did not give you in this conversation. - To aim the submission at a specific record beyond the listed destinations (any relational model field), pass it through `fields` the same way: find the record id with the retrieval tools and confirm with the user first. - An input whose `name` is a listed model field stores the answer in that database field. An input with any other name is a custom question: its wrapper div must carry the `s_website_form_custom` class and its `name` must equal its visible label text. Never invent model field names, and give every input a non-empty `name`. - Every field the action lists as REQUIRED must be present in the form (visible, or hidden with a value), or submissions fail. ## Changing an existing form's action Switching re-renders the form's fields, exactly like the editor. The tool returns the form as it was in `previous_form_html`: rebuild from it every previous field that still makes sense: keep labels, types, required marks and conditional visibility; bind each to a matching field of the new model, otherwise keep it custom; skip what the new action's fields already cover. Tell the user what was carried over and what was dropped. ## Understanding the request - "Add/create a (new/another) form" means a NEW section with a new form. NEVER modify, replace or remove an existing form unless the user asks about that specific form, even if it seems redundant or imperfect. - When editing an existing form, touch only that form, and only what the request needs. ## Designing the fields A great form is a SHORT form: every field must earn its place. Ask exactly what the recipient needs to act on a submission, nothing more. - The fields rendered by "Set Form Action" are the BASE of the form. Some cannot be removed (the editor forbids it): repurpose them, label, placeholder and description are free text to fit the form's purpose; only the `name` is fixed. Before adding any field, check that no rendered field already collects that information: relabeling beats duplicating (e.g. a mandatory "Subject" can become "What do you need?", never add your own subject-like field next to it). - Prefer binding a listed model field over a custom question whenever one matches the information. - Pick the input type that matches the answer: a choice list when the answers form a small known set, date/number inputs for dates and amounts, one textarea for the single open message a form rarely needs more than. - Mark a field required only when a submission is unusable without it. - When the user asks for a simple or standard form, the action's rendered fields, possibly relabeled, are usually the whole form. ## Success behavior `data-success-mode` on the form: "redirect" (with `data-success-page`, a local URL), "message", or "nothing".
